# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.

# Research Report: `/app/categorizationapp` — Indian Bank Statement Transaction Categorization Library

All paths below are absolute; line numbers refer to the current files on disk. Nothing was modified.

---

## 1. Overall Architecture

### Layout

```
/app/categorizationapp/
├── setup.py                                (packaging + deps)
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── __init__.py                         (Flask app creation, request timing hooks)
    ├── Controller.py                       (Flask routes; per-bank dispatch pipeline)
    ├── BankScripts/                        (35 bank-specific categorizers: SBI, HDFC, ICICI, IDBI, Axis, ...)
    └── UtilityScripts/                     (shared, bank-agnostic passes + regex constants)
        ├── AppUtil.py                      (df cleanup, sep_by_* splitters, py_extract, fuzzy_match)
        ├── RegexConstants.py / BankRegexConstants.py  (large regex constant dictionaries)
        ├── Purpose.py / CardPurpose.py     (transactionSubcategory assignment)
        ├── CleanName.py / CardCleanNames.py (payee/"clean name" normalization)
        ├── InternalPayment.py              (self-transfer detection via fuzzy name match)
        ├── SalaryDetection.py, PFMCategorization.py, SimpleDescription.py, RecurrentTxns.py
        └── TransactionCategoryEnums.py / TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py (display-name enums)
```

### Flask app & entry points

`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py`:
- Line 7: `app = Flask(__name__)`; lines 15–24 add before/after request timing hooks; line 28: `import categorizationapp.Controller` registers routes. Line 30–31 contains an `app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=9898, debug=True)` guard (only effective if the module were executed directly, which is unusual for a package `__init__`).

`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` exposes three routes:
- Line 51–53: `GET /` — health check.
- Line 55–67: `POST /recurrentTransactions` — normalizes `requestPayload['transactions']` into a DataFrame and calls `recurrent_transactions`.
- Line 69–936: `POST /categorizeTransaction` — the main entry point. Reads `bank`, `acc_type` (line 75), `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, converts the transactions JSON to a pandas DataFrame (line 81), cleans it via `AppUtil.clean_input_df` (line 87), then dispatches through a giant `if/elif` ladder on `bank` (lines 91–930; one nearly-identical block per bank, e.g. `"SBI"` at 115, `"ICICI"` at 139, `"HDFC"` at 163, `"IDBI"` at 235, `"AXIS"` at 427, ending with `"TAMILNAD_MERCANTILE"` at 907; unknown bank → error at 931–932). Result serialized at 935–936.

### The per-bank pipeline (identical in each branch; e.g. SBI at 115–138)

1. **Bank script** — `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` from `BankScripts/`. Each script builds a `conditions_choices` list of `[boolean-Series, choice]` pairs, evaluated with `np.select` (first matching rule wins, default `"TRANSFER"`), producing:
   - `transactionCategory` (e.g. `UPI`, `NEFT`, `CHEQUE_PAID`, `AUTO_PAYMENT`, `REFUND`…)
   - `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`
   - `partyName` (raw payee extracted from the narration via `sep_by_*` splitters or `py_extract` regexes), then `party2` = `partyName` without spaces (e.g. IDBI.py:128).
2. **If `acc_type == "CREDIT_CARD"`**: `card_clean_names(transactions)` (`UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py`) then `card_purpose(transactions)` (`UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py`).
3. `purpose(transactions, accountType)` (`UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:9`) — cross-bank subcategory rules (SALARY, INSURANCE, LOAN_REPAYMENT, CREDIT_CARD_PAYMENT, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE, …), many gated on `accountType=="SAVING"` / `"CURRENT"`.
4. `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` (`UtilityScripts/CleanName.py:9`, 1971 lines) — maps raw `partyName`/description fragments to canonical merchant names ("Airtel DTH", "Adani Electricity", "HDFC Bank Loan …", etc.).
5. If `accountHolder` given: `internal_payment(...)` (`UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py:8`) — fuzzy-matches (fuzzywuzzy, ratio > 75; AppUtil.py:48–51) the account-holder name against `partyName` for categories in the whitelist at InternalPayment.py:15 and marks `transactionSubcategory="INTERNAL_PAYMENT"` / `isInternalPayment="true"` (lines 55–60), excluding `["INWARD_BOUNCE","CHEQUE_RETURN","REVERSAL"]` (line 16).
6. If `acc_type == "SAVING"`: `salary_detection(transactions)` (recurrence-based salary detection using scipy/sklearn in `SalaryDetection.py`).
7. If `isPFMEnabled`: `pfm_categorization` (PFM buckets like SHOPPING, BILL_PAYMENT — `PFMCategorization.py:8`) and `simple_description` (`SimpleDescription.py`).

**How a transaction gets a category:** its `description` (narration) and sometimes `remark` and `amount`/`type` columns are run through the ordered regex rule list in its bank's script; the first matching rule's label becomes `transactionCategory`, default `"TRANSFER"`.

**How it gets a "clean name"/payee:** the bank script first extracts a raw `partyName` by splitting the narration on a delimiter (`sep_by_` = split on `/`, `sep_by_dash` = split on `-`, `sep_by_wave` = `~`, `sep_by_colon`, `sep_by_star`, etc., AppUtil.py:14–45) or via `py_extract` (regex group extraction with NaN-handling, AppUtil.py:61–66). Then `CleanName.clean_names` (or `CardCleanNames` for CC) rewrites the raw name to a canonical merchant name.

---

## 2. Cheque Detection — narration/remark that is ONLY a cheque number

The dominant pattern: many banks treat a `remark` column that is *only digits of a fixed width* as the cheque number, assigning `CHEQUE_PAID` (debit) / `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` (credit). Exact regexes:

| File:Line | Exact regex | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/PNB.py:60` | `"^[0-9]{5,6}$"` | `remark` match + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID` |
| `PNB.py:61` | `"^[0-9]{5,6}$"` | remark + CREDIT → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` |
| `PNB.py:55` | `"^[0-9]{6}"` (remark) + `"CASH WITHDRA?WAL"` (description) | → `CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL` |
| `PNB.py:46` | `"^[0-9]{6}$"` (remark) + `"\\bFD\\b"` desc | → `FIXED_DEPOSIT` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/Axis.py:58–59` | `"^[0-9]{5,6}$"` | remark, DEBIT→`CHEQUE_PAID` / CREDIT→`CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/BankOfMaharashtra.py:73–74` | `"^[0-9]{5,6}$"` | same pattern |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/YES.py:52–53` | `"^[0-9]{3,6}$"` | same pattern |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/UCO.py:44–45` | `"^[0-9]{3,6}$"` | same pattern |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/Kotak.py:65,67` | `"^[0-9]{3,5}$"` | remark, CREDIT→deposit (65) / DEBIT→paid (67) |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/KarurVyasa.py:50–51` | `"^00[0-9]{4}$"` | 6 digits with leading `00` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/RBL.py:49–50` | `"^[0-9]{1,3}$"` | short cheque serials |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/Indusind.py:64` | `"^[0-9]{5}$"` | remark, DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/SouthIndian.py:32` | `"[0-9]{6}"` | remark, DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID` (unanchored!) |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/TamilnadMerchantile.py:33–34` | `"^[0-9]{5,}/"` | remark starting with 5+ digits + `/` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/HDFC.py:100` | `"^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}"` + `remark.str.len().eq(16)` | 16-char zero-padded cheque no. → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/UCO.py:38` | `"^[A-Z].*[0-9]{2,6}$"` | *description* ending in cheque digits, DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID` |

Description-based near-misses worth knowing:
- `/app/.../BankScripts/IDBI.py:56` — `"[0-9]{6}-|^WTHDRL,CLG|CHQ Paid"` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`; line 58 — `"[0-9]{6}-|^BY INST|CHQ\\s?DEP"` + CREDIT → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` (6 digits followed by a dash anywhere in the description).
- `IDBI.py:55/57` — a description that is letters-only (contains `"[A-Z]+"`, contains **no** digits and **no** punctuation) is treated as a cheque payee name: DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`, CREDIT → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`.
- `/app/.../BankScripts/SBI.py:47` — `"\\bCH [0-9]{6}-"` + CREDIT → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`.

For clean names when the narration is just a cheque number:
- `IDBI.py:109`: `remark.str.contains("[0-9]{4,6}")` & category in `["CHEQUE_PAID","CHEQUE_DEPOSIT"]` → `partyName = transactions.description` (the description carries the payee).
- `Kotak.py:241`: `CHEQUE_PAID` & remark `"^[0-9]{3,5}$"` → `partyName = description`.
- `UnionBank.py:122`: category `TRANSFER` & remark `"^[0-9]{6}$"` → `partyName = description`.
- `PNB.py:162`: description with no digits/punct/lowercase & category cheque → `partyName = description`.
- `Indusind.py:190`: cheque category, description has no digits, remark `"[0-9]{5,}"` → `partyName = description`.

Note also `/app/.../BankScripts/HDFC.py:124`: a **description** that is exactly six digits (`"^[0-9]{6}$"`) on a CREDIT in a SAVING account flips `TRANSFER` → `SALARY` (not cheque) — relevant if you're testing 6-digit-only narrations on HDFC.

---

## 3. NACH / ACH Narration Parsing (e.g. `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES`)

### Categorization (IDBI is the bank whose format matches `ACH-BD-...`)

`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py`:
- Line 14: `"^ACH|^ETPC ACH"` + CREDIT → `AUTO_CREDIT`
- Line 38: `"\\bACH-|Direct Debit|^NACH"` + DEBIT → `AUTO_PAYMENT`
- Line 24: `"DIRDB REVERESED|RVSL ACH"` + CREDIT → `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`

### Payee extraction for `ACH-…` narrations — IDBI.py lines 81–88 (dash-token slicing via `sep_by_dash(description, n1, n2)` = `description.split('-')[n1:n2]`):

```python
81: [transactions.description.str.contains("\\bETPC.*ACH-BD-", ...) , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,2,3)],
82: [transactions.description.str.contains("\\bETPC.*ACH-", ...)    , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,1,2)],
83: [transactions.description.str.contains("^ACH-BD-NACH", ...)     , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,2,3)],
84: [transactions.description.str.contains("^ACH-BD-", ...)         , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,2,3)],
85: [transactions.description.str.contains("^ACH-BARB-", ...)       , sep_by_dash(transactions.description, 2, 3)],
86: [transactions.description.str.contains("^ACH-", ...)            , sep_by_dash(transactions.description, 1, 2)],
87: [transactions.description.str.contains("^NACH,", ...)           , sep_by_wave(transactions.description,1,2)],
88: [transactions.description.str.contains("^NACH", ...)            , sep_by_(transactions.description,1,2)],
```

**Important behavioral detail for your exact example:** for `"ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES"`, line 83 matches first and `sep_by_dash(desc, 2, 3)` returns token index 2 = `"NACH"`, *not* `"ACME INDUSTRIES"` (which is token 3). The employer/payee at the end is only extracted correctly by line 84's rule when the narration is `ACH-BD-<NAME>` (token 2 = name). So the `^ACH-BD-NACH` rule at line 83 appears to slice the wrong token (arguably should be `sep_by_dash(...,3,4)`); after `.str.title()` at IDBI.py:116 the partyName would be `"Nach"`. (It is then not blanked by the cleanup rule at IDBI.py:122, which only blanks single letters/pure digits/`Xidb...`.)

### Other banks' NACH/ACH parsing (extraction logic with groups):

- `/app/.../BankScripts/YES.py:77–94` — a ladder of `^ACH DR TP ACH (.*) [0-9]+`, `ACH DR TP EMANDATE (.*) [0-9]` (line 80), `ACH DR BD (.*) [A-Z0-9]{10,12}` (86), `ACH DR BD-` → `sep_by_dash(desc,1,2)` (87), `ACH DR BARB (.*)` (90), all via `py_extract(..., index=0)`.
- `/app/.../BankScripts/Kotak.py:124–135` — e.g. line 124 `"^NACH-SAL-CR-SAL-"` → `sep_by_dash(desc,4,5)`; line 125 `"^NACH-[A-Z0-9]+-CR-"` → `sep_by_dash(desc,3,4)`; line 128 `"NACH-RPN-DR-TP ACH"` → `py_extract(pat="TP ACH(.*)-", index=0)`; line 134 `"NACH-10-DR-BD-|NACH-10-DR-BARB-"` → `sep_by_dash(desc,4,5)`; line 135 `"^NACH-10-DR-|NACH-LEG-DR-"` → `sep_by_dash(desc,3,4)`.
- `/app/.../BankScripts/PNB.py:142–143` — `"^NACH/"` CREDIT → `sep_by_(desc,3,4)`; `"^ACH/|\\bACH/|NACH-DR/|^ECS|NACH- DR/"` → `sep_by_(desc,1,2)`.
- `/app/.../BankScripts/StandardCharted.py:119–122` — `"NACH DR IW:"` → `sep_by_colon(desc,2,3)`/(1,2); line 122: contains `"NACH (.*) [A-z]{4}[0-9]{14}"` → `py_extract(pat="[0-9]{16} (.*) [A-z]{4}[0-9]{14}", index=0)` (name sandwiched between a 16-digit mandate number and a 4-letter+14-digit UMRN).
- `/app/.../BankScripts/BOI.py:67–68` — `py_extract(pat="NACH DR INW - (.*) [0-9]+", index=0)` and the CR variant.
- `/app/.../BankScripts/BOB.py:106–107` — `"^NACH DR INW"` → `py_extract(pat="-(.+) [0-9]", index=0)`.
- `/app/.../BankScripts/Saraswat.py:68` — `"ACH-"` → `sep_by_dash(desc, 2, 3)`.
- `/app/.../BankScripts/UnionBank.py:78–79` — `"^NACH/[0-9]"` → `sep_by_(desc,2,3)`; `"^NACH/"` → `sep_by_(desc,1,2)`.
- `/app/.../BankScripts/IDFC.py:76,80` — `"NACH/"` → `sep_by_(desc,1,2)`; `"NACH~"` → `sep_by_wave(desc,1,2)`.
- `/app/.../BankScripts/Karnataka.py:58` — AUTO_PAYMENT + `"-NACH-"` → `sep_by_(sep_by_dash(desc,3,4), 0, 1)`.
- `/app/.../BankScripts/ICICI.py:137–138` — `NACH_AD_RTN_CHRG~…` → `sep_by_wave(desc,4,5)` / `(1,2)`.
- CleanName layer: `/app/.../UtilityScripts/CleanName.py:602` (`"NACH- DR/EQUITAS"` → "Equitas Bank Loan " + `sep_by_(desc,2,3)`), 1747 (`"^NACH-DR/HDFC BANK LIMITED/0"` → "HDFC Bank Loan " + `sep_by_(desc,2,3)`), 1756 (Indusind analog).

---

## 4. "Short block of letters + long digit string + name" (e.g. `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`)

The exact match for your example is in IDBI:

- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py:110`:
  ```python
  [transactions.description.str.contains("^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}", na=False, case=False) ,
      py_extract(transactions.description, pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)],
  ```
  Detection regex: `"^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}"` — 5 uppercase letters then ≥10 digits at start (matches `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`). Extraction: `py_extract(pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)`. **Likely bug:** the extract pattern has only one capture group (index 0). `py_extract` (AppUtil.py:61–66) does `str.extract(...).get(index)`; `get(1)` returns `None`, so it returns `pd.Series("")` — the name (`RAVI KUMAR`) is never actually extracted; `index=0` would return it.
  - Follow-up cleanup at IDBI.py:120–121 handles `partyName == "Na"` cases with `"/INST/NEFT/[0-9]+/[0-9]+ (.+)"` and `"/INST/NEFT/[0-9]+/([A-Z]+)[0-9]"` extractions.

## 5. Auto-debit Mandate "Token" Verification Charges (small nominal amount + mandate keyword)

There is no literal "token" keyword (only `AMC SOFT TOKEN` inside `BANK_CHARGES_HDFC`, BankRegexConstants.py:105). The token/₹1–₹2 mandate-verification debits are handled by amount-gated rules:

**Classified as ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION (verification, small fixed amount + mandate keyword):**
- `/app/.../BankScripts/Indusind.py:30`:
  ```python
  [transactions.amount.eq(2) & transactions.description.str.contains("MANDATE|Mandate", na=False, case=False), "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
  ```
  (also line 29: `BANK_VER` regex + `amount.isin([1,-1])`; line 31: any ₹1 DEBIT → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`)
- `/app/.../BankScripts/Axis.py:25`:
  ```python
  [transactions.amount.eq(1) & transactions.description.str.contains("MANDATE|Mandate", na=False, case=False), "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
  ```
  (line 24: `BANK_VER` + `amount.isin([1,-1])`; line 26: any ₹1 CREDIT)
- The generic verification keyword list is `BANK_VER` at `/app/.../UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py:327` (`"PennyD rop|Accou|Test Pa|AccVeri|...|ny\\s?drop"`), used with `amount.isin([1,-1])` in HDFC.py:13 (`amount.lt(2)`), IDBI.py:12, BOB.py:12, Indusind.py:29, Axis.py:24, etc.
- Cross-bank fallback: `/app/.../UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:165` — `transactionSubcategory == "LOAN"` & `amount ∈ {1,-1}` → subcategory `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`.

**Classified as AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES (mandate registration/verification fees, amount-capped):**
- `/app/.../BankScripts/SBI.py:33`:
  ```python
  ["^ACH MANDATE CHARGE|E mandate|\\bACH\\b CHARGE?" ... & type=="DEBIT" & amount.lt(150), "AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES"],
  ```

## 6. Card Refund vs Card Reversal — account-type dependence

The only place where account type directly decides refund vs card reversal is IndusInd:

`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py:26–27`:
```python
26: [transactions.description.str.contains("\\bPOS TXN",na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT")
        & transactions.amount.ge(10) & (accountType=="SAVINGS") , "CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL"],
27: [transactions.description.str.contains("\\bPOS TXN",na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT")
        & (accountType=="SAVING") , "REFUND"],
```
- Intended logic: for savings accounts, a POS credit ≥ ₹10 = `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`, smaller ones = `REFUND`.

In a CURRENT account, neither fires (falls through; the subcategory rule at Indusind.py:95 gives `"^POS TXN-"` credits in CURRENT accounts subcategory `CARD_RECEIPTS`).

**Tests: none.** `glob **/*test*` returns nothing; the repo contains only `setup.py` and the package (git history is a single commit `fc21c7f "import codebase"`). There is no README, no requirements.txt, no CI config, no `run.py`/`wsgi.py`.

steps.message:
All five reported failures are root-caused, fixed, and verified. Summary for the incident record:

## Root causes and fixes (5 defects, 3 files, 4 lines total)

**1. Cheque filed as generic transfer when the note is just the cheque number** — `BankScripts/Indusind.py:64`
The remark-based cheque rule matched only exactly-5-digit remarks (`^[0-9]{5}$`), so a 6-digit cheque number (standard width; also why "earlier cheques were tagged correctly") fell through to `TRANSFER`. The bank's own payee rule at Indusind.py:190 expects `[0-9]{5,}`, and sibling banks (Axis, PNB, BOM) all use `^[0-9]{5,6}$`. Fixed to `^[0-9]{5,6}$`.

**2. Salary payee shows `NACH` instead of employer for `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES`** — `BankScripts/IDBI.py:83`
The `^ACH-BD-NACH` rule sliced dash-token 2 (`NACH`) instead of token 3 (the name). Fixed to match `^ACH-BD-NACH-` and slice token 3. Narrations like `ACH-BD-NACHIKET SHARMA` (a payee whose name merely starts with "NACH") now fall through to the `^ACH-BD-` rule and still resolve identically to before.

**3. Blank sender name for `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR` references** — `BankScripts/IDBI.py:110`
`py_extract(pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)` asked for capture group 1 of a single-group pattern; `py_extract` (AppUtil.py:61) returns an empty series for a missing group, so the name was always dropped. Fixed to `index=0`.

**4. Mandate token confirmation charge filed as transfer instead of verification** — `BankScripts/BankOfMaharashtra.py:36-37`
`amount.isin(["1","-1"])` compared the numeric `amount` column (coerced in `clean_input_df`, AppUtil.py:9) against string literals — both `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` rules were dead code, so the ₹1 mandate-verification debit fell to `TRANSFER`. Fixed to numeric `[1,-1]` / `[1]`.

**5. Card reversal shown as plain refund, dependent on account category** — `BankScripts/Indusind.py:26`
The `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` rule compared against `"SAVINGS"` while the service passes `"SAVING"` (see Controller.py and the neighboring rule on line 27), so it could never fire and every POS-credit ≥ ₹10 fell into the `REFUND` rule. Fixed the literal to `"SAVING"`.

## Verification
- A harness (`/tmp/opencode/repro.py`) reproduced all 5 failures verbatim pre-fix (e.g. `Nach` payee, empty name, `TRANSFER` instead of `CHEQUE_PAID`/`ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`/`CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`), and all 8 incident assertions pass post-fix.
- A 30-row snapshot of ordinary transactions (UPI, NEFT, IMPS, POS, ATM, cash deposits, interest, 5-digit cheques, ₹2 mandate tokens, existing NACH/ACH forms, CURRENT-account card receipts) recorded before the fix is **byte-identical** after the fix — no currently-correct transaction moves.
- End-to-end run through the Flask `/categorizeTransaction` route (including Purpose/CleanName/InternalPayment passes) confirms correct output at the API level. (The `SalaryDetection` tracebacks in that run are pre-existing and caused only by my minimal payload omitting `transactionDate`; the Controller already tolerates that failure.)
